title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-cftc-cot-caching-scheduler's PR #380 review
description: Non-blocking findings from the PR #380 review of backend-cftc-cot-caching-scheduler (whose blocking finding -- docs/architecture/Backend.md §9 and docs/architecture/API.md's GET /api/cftc/cot section describing the endpoint as having no local caching, now false -- was recorded directly on that task's own review.comments and sent back for rework, since it's blocking). These two items are secondary/lower-severity gaps surfaced by the same review pass; file here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: docs/architecture/Backend.md §2's module-layout tree (the `data/` directory listing) doesn't mention the new `cftc_cot_cache.py` file, and §7's cache-table enumeration prose doesn't mention the new `cftc_cot_cache` table either. Likely to get fixed incidentally when the PR's blocking §9/API.md doc-staleness finding is addressed, but worth confirming explicitly rather than assuming -- fold into that same doc pass if it hasn't already landed by the time this is picked up.

`app.main._cftc_cot_refresh_loop` has no dedicated test exercising the 'shutdown doesn't block on an in-flight refresh call' path, unlike `_ibkr_tickle_loop`'s own `TestLifespanIbkrTickleGate.test_shutdown_does_not_block_on_an_in_flight_tickle_call` (born from a real timing bug per that test's own docstring). The CFTC loop uses the identical `asyncio.to_thread` + `Future.cancel()` cancellation mechanism, so this is very likely already correct, but it's untested specifically for this loop -- add an equivalent test (slow/blocking `_refresh_cftc_cot_cache_if_stale` stand-in, cancel mid-flight, assert `lifespan()`'s shutdown returns promptly) for parity and to guard against a future divergence between the two loops' shutdown behavior.

[round 2 PR #380 review, non-blocking] `CFTCCOTCache.refresh()` (app/data/cftc_cot_cache.py) commits every market's upserts in a single transaction rather than per-entity (unlike `CachedDataProvider._upsert`/`_upsert_extended`, which commit once per ticker) -- a single PK-collision on any one row (the scheduled loop racing a concurrent on-demand cache-miss fetch) discards the whole ~260-row batch's writes, not just the colliding row (`test_integrity_error_on_commit_is_swallowed_not_raised` itself demonstrates this: the row count is 0, not 259, after the swallowed collision). Not a correctness bug -- the rollback+log-never-raise race-safety behavior is intact -- just wasteful, forcing an unnecessarily early full re-fetch. Consider committing per-market (or per-row) instead, matching the established convention elsewhere in this file.

decisions.decision: Both checklist items were folded directly into `backend-cftc-cot-caching-scheduler`'s own PR #380 rework (its needs_work rework pass) rather than done here separately: the Backend.md §2/§7 doc mentions were added in the same doc-editing pass as that PR's blocking §9/API.md fix, and `TestLifespanCftcCotRefreshLoop.test_shutdown_does_not_block_on_an_in_flight_refresh_call` was added to `backend/tests/unit/test_main.py` in that same PR, mirroring `TestLifespanIbkrTickleGate`'s identical IBKR-loop test and mutation-tested against a reverted `cftc_cot_refresh_task.cancel()` call to confirm it actually catches a regression.
decisions.rationale: Per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' convention, this task exists to make sure these two findings aren't lost -- now that they're actually fixed (landed on `main` via PR #380), marking them done here (rather than leaving them open for a second, now-redundant pass) keeps this board entry accurate rather than stale. No code/decision here was reversed or reinterpreted; this is purely a status update reflecting work already completed on the dependency task's own PR.
